question: Does retaining the response weight at the time each mean-input change occurred repair the strong-input termination error, without new coefficients or changes to static and first-order response?
hypothesis: Existing closure multiplies all accumulated mean memory by the current (or filtered-current) alpha. A moving working point can therefore reweight old input history instantaneously. Test weighting mean increments before the same causal exponential memory filter.
equations: p_dot=-p/tau_s+(1-alpha(workpoint(t)))*mu_dot; mu_eff=mu-p+eta_E*(vE-vEf)+eta_I*(vI-vIf). The same existing variance readout and static transfer are retained.
prediction: No new coefficient, pole, time constant or selected optimum. Both variants are diagnostics on already acquired targets; no held-out acceptance claim.
checks: Constant alpha identity to original input mixture under fixed weights
Small perturbation first-order identity with original response, including amplitude halving
Rates within zero and refractory bounds without post-hoc clipping
scope: Two zero-fit local nonlinear closure diagnostics motivated by new mean/variance counterfactual evidence. This does not repair existing small-signal validation failures, constitute fresh held-out validation, deploy a spatial model or classify onset. If no variant passes every selected full/mean/variance waveform, do not launch a network with it.
budget: Two fixed variants on the two existing 12-condition input sets; no new Monte Carlo or network run.
